newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: CRICKET-FLEMING SAVES NEW ZEALAND FROM COLLAPSE.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-FLEMING SAVES NEW ZEALAND FROM COLLAPSE.

text.p: New Zealand reached a fighting first innings score of 215 for eight thanks to an 81-run eighth-wicket stand between Stephen Fleming and skipper Lee Germon on the first day of the second test on Thursday.

The start of the match was delayed for 20 minutes because new balls had not arrived on time and 25 minutes more were wasted when Fleming protested that sun was disturbing his vision just after tea break.

When stumps were drawn, Germon was a gutsy 45 not out and Dipak Patel six not out as New Zealand sought to complete a 2-0 series win over Pakistan after winning the first test in Lahore earlier this week
The day belonged to Pakistan's googly specialist Mushtaq Ahmad and test debutant Mohammad Zahid, who shared the eight wickets which fell.
Mushtaq took four of the five wickets which fell after lunch and finished the day with five for 73 in 26 overs.
Zahid, a 20-year-old right-arm fast medium bowler, claimed three for 51 and had two wickets in the space of seven deliveries before lunch.
Bryan Young and Justin Vaughan put on 33 for the opening wicket before New Zealand collapsed to 111 for seven.
Young batted convincingly before Mushtaq had him leg before for 39, which included five boundaries.
Adam Parore went lbw to Zahid for three and then Mushtaq claimed the wickets of Nathan Astle and Mark Greatbatch as New Zealand reeled at 87 for five.
Fleming and Chris Cairns, who had shared a decisive 141-run sixth wicket partnership in the first test at Lahore, brought the 100 up.
But, with 110 on the board, Cairns was brilliantly caught at silly point by Mohammad Wasim off Mushtaq for nine.
One run later Zahid trapped Chris Harris leg before.
But Germon and Fleming stopped the collapse. Fleming was eventually bowled by Mushtaq for 67, including 11 fours, scored off 110 balls in 208 minutes.
An over before the close Germon was lucky when Saeed Anwar dropped him at first slip off Salim Malik.
